worker_limits: No browsing, command execution, file modification, or test execution was performed.
All statements below are derived only from the supplied line-numbered files.
No claim is made that any simulation, build, BIT, board, or MIG test passed in this task.
Innovation judgment is not decided here; potential new observability is noted but not endorsed.

findings.title: DS-priority experiments have different fixtures and versions and cannot be stitched causally
findings.claim: The PN/N/DS-priority evidence comes from at least two different experiment regimes. The §8 model DS-read-priority intervention removed the model PN degradation, while the §29 DS-return-priority run still left PN slower. They must not be combined into one causal story.
evidence: docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:88-95: §8 uses real two iDMA, banked controller, TL, DS_if, fixed 50/50 delayer and shared xbar; FIFO model P=91878 PN=93480 (+1.744%), window DS-read-priority P=79847 PN=79484 (-0.455%); DS priority only changes C++ DDR cross-ID return order, preserves same-ID order and backpressured VALID data, and does not change RTL or warmup.

docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:15-22: §29 reuses frozen old binary without rebuild; only +ds-priority=0 to 1 and CSV output path changed; one 64-bit R port at most one beat/cycle, shared queue cap 16, no second DDR port; serial P=92109 PN=92374 (+265, 0.288%), DS-return-priority P=88989 PN=91547 (+2558, 2.875%).

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:97: in the §8 DS-priority model, both modes' 93 DS reads have latency sum 2976 and 32 cycles each; A PTW-active is 13489 in both modes; model PN degradation disappeared.

docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:24: in §29, DS AR-to-first-R mean/max are both 32 cycles and A PTW-active is 13489 in both modes, but PN is still slower by 2558 cycles; this is not evidence that full translation or preparation timing is identical.
findings.uncertainty: The two experiments differ in binary/fixture state and queue/credit point. No shared causal ledger is supplied. The §8 disappearance of model PN degradation cannot be transferred to §29 or to board behavior.

findings.title: N early payload delaying PTE wait is model-reachable, not complete board causation
findings.claim: The supplied evidence supports a model-reachable mechanism: in PN, early V data traffic can delay an A page-table PTE return in the shared DDR model. It does not prove the complete board PN slowdown or that MIG FIFO ordering is the root cause.
evidence: docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:99: PN V fast response at 2758/2764; V data read enters DDR at 2763 (ID32, 0x80000000, 256 beats); A leaf PTE read enters at 2766 (ID48, 0x70010, 1 beat); PTE returns at 3100, taking 334 cycles, and fills at 3156. In P the same PTE enters at 2763, returns at 2808 (45 cycles), fills at 2864; V data read then enters at 2876.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:101-103: evidence files are out/pn-data-path-20261007/comparison.json, trace-evidence.json, p-full-events.csv, pn-full-events.csv, acceptance.json, source-provenance.json; only model and workload reachability is proved; board PN is about 12.74% slower while this model is 1.744% slower; DDR-priority intervention also changed synthetic CPU read counts, so all CPU factors are not isolated and no definite algorithm bug is shown.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:127,131: board gap0 PN still has V slower and A slower; V9 has no PTW occupancy or page-table AR/R independent timing counters; sharedAWwait only counts tr-entry valid && !ready; board evidence is compatible with downstream contention but does not alone prove MIG return FIFO or PTE blocked by data burst.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:193: P/PN's 93 DDR DS reads use only 6 distinct PTE word addresses; 0x30000 and 0x60800 each occur 31 times; four leaf PTEs occur 8/8/8/7 times; 62/93 are repeated upper-level accesses, but this is not a promised cycle-saving ratio.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:415: in one old cold-page trajectory, a 256-beat data read persists after root return from 1327 to 1582; the next-level PTE waits from 1408 to 1653, 245 cycles versus root 32 cycles, and CPU reads also affect the interval; this cannot all be attributed to that one read.
findings.uncertainty: The board-vs-model gap is large and unresolved. The supplied sources do not prove MIG return FIFO behavior, do not isolate CPU interference, and do not quantify full PN slowdown from the PTE-delay mechanism alone.

findings.title: The supplied DS PTE interface does not expose requesting DMA or access type
findings.claim: In the supplied rv_iommu_ds_if.sv wrapper, DS requests are merged from internal IOMMU clients and returns are demuxed by AXI ID only. There is no port or explicit field for requesting DMA/DID or access type at this wrapper.
evidence: cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/ext_interfaces/rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:30-75: module ports are axi_req_t/axi_resp_t for DS and internal clients; no DID or ttype port is present.

cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/ext_interfaces/rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:77-93: AR stream_arbiter merges seven internal DS clients: DDTW, PDTW, PTW, CQ, PQ, MSIPTW, MRIF handler; the arbiter output is ar_data/ar_valid/ar_ready.

cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/ext_interfaces/rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:221-247: R responses are assigned to all internal resp.r fields as r_data, but valid/ready are demuxed by r_data.id: id 0=PTW, 1=DDTW, 2=PDTW, 3=CQ, 4=MSIPTW, 5=MRIF, default PTW.
cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/translation_logic/rv_iommu_ptw.sv:51-54: PTW has is_store_i and is_rx_i indicating access type internally, plus en_1S_i/en_2S_i.
cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/translation_logic/rv_iommu_ptw.sv:59-61: PTW has iova_i, pscid_i, gscid_i, but not an explicit DMA DID at this interface.

cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/translation_logic/rv_iommu_ptw.sv:275-282: PTW AR defaults set mem_req_o.ar.id = 0, so at the shared DS return path PTW responses can be identified by AXI ID 0, not by an explicit requester DMA/access-type field.
findings.uncertainty: Upstream rv_iommu_top or transaction-controller code may carry DID/ttype in AXI user bits or context, but that is not visible in the supplied DS IF file. From the supplied file alone, the DS PTE wrapper only gives AXI-ID/channel origin.

findings.title: Current W owner, missing payload, FIFO state, and source-R visibility are not fully present in supplied files
findings.claim: The supplied files show DS-internal W-owner FIFO logic and iDMA payload transport buffering, but they do not expose a complete production view of current payload W owner, missing payload/frontier, or source-R visibility to the IOMMU service decision.
evidence: cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/ext_interfaces/rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:111-219: DS IF has an internal W-owner selector FIFO for DS internal AW clients (CQ, FQ, PQ, MRIF, MSI IG); aw_ready requires !w_fifo_full; AWID is pushed on accepted AW and popped on W last; w_valid requires !w_fifo_empty. This is not the external DMA payload W path.

cva6/corev_apu/fpga/src/ariane_peripherals_xilinx.sv:1255-1310: actual iDMA instance parameters include BUFFER_DEPTH 512 for i<2 in nonblock mode else 3, NUM_AX_IN_FLIGHT 8, MEM_SYS_DEPTH 0, RAW_COUPLING_AVAIL 0, DEVICE_ID 10+i, PROCESS_ID 20+i, AxID '0.
cva6/corev_apu/fpga/src/ariane_peripherals_xilinx.sv:1465-1467: fullbuffer_jobs_i is connected only from fullbuffer_jobs[1:0] in nonblock mode; only DMA0/1 have the prototype whole-copy buffers.
cva6/corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_axi_transport_layer.sv:199-202: read AR is directly connected to AXI; ar_ready_o is axi_rsp_i.ar_ready.
cva6/corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_axi_transport_layer.sv:289-291: write AW is directly connected to AXI; aw_ready_o is axi_rsp_i.aw_ready.
cva6/corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_axi_transport_layer.sv:314-360: write is decoupled from read; ready_to_write depends on buffer_out_valid and mask_out; axi_req_o.w_valid is ready_to_write or write_q.

cva6/corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_axi_transport_layer.sv:468-492: idma_buffer is instantiated; buffer_busy_o is !buffer_clean. The module provides rdata_o/rdata_valid_o to the DMA datapath, not an explicit source-R owner/address visible to IOMMU.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:170: production current-owner, AW-first, and cross-bank gates are cited as rv_iommu_banked_ctl.sv:246-278, rv_iommu_trans_ctl_wrap.sv:623-647, and axi_demux_simple.sv:175-177, but those source files are not supplied here.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:197-202: banked control single-owner read admission, bank tags/RR/routing, AW-first behavior, physical AR/AW issue after translation, and iDMA virtual AR path are cited, but exact current signals are not in the supplied files.
findings.uncertainty: The exact current payload W owner, missing-payload condition, FIFO occupancy, and source-R visibility must be read from the cited banked_ctl/trans_ctl_wrap/axi_demux/idma_backend/idma_channel_coupler files. Supplied sources are insufficient to decide them.

findings.title: DS and comp ultimately share downstream DDR/MIG service, but not the payload byte-credit pool
findings.claim: The DS translation path and the comp DMA payload path are separate initiator ports and separate credit domains, even though they eventually share downstream DRAM/clock-converter/MIG service. PTE returns must not be counted as payload byte credit.
evidence: docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:7: production four iDMA enter IOMMU via ariane_peripherals_xilinx.sv:1228-1252; data returns via comp to system interconnect; DS passes through a separate delayer to another initiator port; top level has separate comp/DS initiator ports but they eventually join the same DRAM target, clock converter, and MIG interface; different initiator ports do not mean different physical DDR bandwidth, and a single R port does not force the current model FIFO behavior on MIG.

docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:9: rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:81-109 and 227-273 merge PTW/DDTW etc. inside DS and share one return stage; DS returns and DMA payload share downstream DDR service but do not share the studied payload byte-credit pool; MaxSlvTrans/MaxMstTrans=8 is a transaction cap, not eight full payload stores.
cva6/corev_apu/fpga/src/ariane_peripherals_xilinx.sv:48-49: iommu_comp and iommu_ds are separate AXI master ports.
cva6/corev_apu/fpga/src/ariane_peripherals_xilinx.sv:1361-1387: DS has separate axi_delayer; comp request/response are separately assigned to iommu_comp.
cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/ext_interfaces/rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:81-109 and 227-273: DS AR arbiter and R return stage merge DDTW/PDTW/PTW/CQ/PQ/MSIPTW/MRIF and demux returns by ID.
findings.uncertainty: The supplied top-level file does not include the MIG/ariane_xilinx.sv lines cited by the document, so the final shared MIG statement is from docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:7, not directly visible in supplied RTL.

findings.title: Accepted AXI transactions and held VALID are immutable; DS priority can only affect not-yet-RVALID or not-yet-offered service
findings.claim: The fixed DS-priority intervention only reorders model DDR returns when no RVALID is held, preserving same-ID order and already-VALID data. It cannot revoke already accepted AXI transactions or alter already offered/held VALID beats.
evidence: docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:15: existing C++ only moves the oldest DS to the head when RVALID is not held; same-ID order is preserved; data already VALID is not changed.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:95: DS-priority intervention only changes C++ DDR cross-ID return order, preserving same-ID order and backpressured VALID data; it does not change RTL or warmup.
cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/ext_interfaces/rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:95-109 and 249-263: DS AR and R use spill_register with Bypass=0, so once accepted a beat is held until handshake.
cva6/corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_axi_transport_layer.sv:199-202 and 289-291: AR and AW are direct AXI connections; once accepted, normal AXI VALID/READY stability applies.
cva6/corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_axi_transport_layer.sv:342-360: write data valid is based on buffer readiness, not a reorderable transaction that can be withdrawn after acceptance.

docs/committed-write-drain-boundary-20261008.md:14,16,22: accepted AW/W obligations, internal A4 count earlier than output handshake, future byte lower bounds, and held AW are tracked separately; output late handshake must not be treated as a new write obligation.
findings.uncertainty: The C++ model can reorder cross-ID returns before RVALID under its local rule. This does not establish that production MIG or interconnect arbitration can make the same choice, nor does it allow revoking accepted transactions.

findings.title: Minimal interface set for a root conditional wait-chain service and the exact current gaps
findings.claim: A root conditional wait-chain service needs handshake-level visibility into PTE progress, payload W owner/frontier, whether a data read is still unoffered, and shared DS/comp admission. The supplied files provide some PTW/DS/iDMA handshakes but miss requester/access-type tagging, comp-side W-owner/payload state, source-R visibility, and MIG arbitration.
evidence: cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/translation_logic/rv_iommu_ptw.sv:100: active_o = state_q != IDLE, giving PTW active state.
cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/translation_logic/rv_iommu_ptw.sv:385-390: MEM_ACCESS asserts mem_req_o.ar_valid and moves to PROC_PTE when mem_resp_i.ar_ready, giving PTE AR offer/accept timing.

cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/translation_logic/rv_iommu_ptw.sv:393-417: PROC_PTE consumes mem_resp_i.r_valid, sets r_ready, checks PTE validity and leaf-ness, giving PTE R return and leaf/nonleaf progress.

cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/translation_logic/rv_iommu_ptw.sv:51-54,59-61: access type is_store_i/is_rx_i and context pscid_i/gscid_i exist inside PTW, but are not exposed at the supplied DS wrapper.
cva6/corev_apu/riscv-iommu/rtl/ext_interfaces/rv_iommu_ds_if.sv:77-93 and 227-273: DS AR arbitration and R return demux give shared DS entry and return by AXI ID, but no requester DMA/access type.

cva6/corev_apu/fpga/src/ariane_peripherals_xilinx.sv:48-49,1228-1253,1361-1387,1404-1467: top level shows separate comp/DS ports, four-DMA TR mux into IOMMU, DS delayer, and IOMMU connections; this is the place to observe comp/DS admission, but the comp-side physical AR/AW generation is not in the supplied files.

cva6/corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_axi_transport_layer.sv:199-202,289-291,314-360,468-492: iDMA exposes AR/AW/R/W/B handshakes and internal buffer/write-readiness, but no source-R owner/address signal to IOMMU.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:170: exact current owner/AW-first/cross-bank sources are cited as rv_iommu_banked_ctl.sv:246-278, rv_iommu_trans_ctl_wrap.sv:623-647, and axi_demux_simple.sv:175-177; these files are not supplied.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:199-200: existing nonblock hit accept/touch and post-translation physical AR/AW issue are cited; accepted OUT responses must be retained, and preserving early translation while delaying physical data needs explicit ready/issue state.

docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:43-50,52,54: G/H discussion requires prepared/independent consumable prefix p, virtual-AR-first-VALID freeze, no truncation of accepted AR, safe fallback when p=0, and rejects mixing PTE return credit with payload credit.
findings.uncertainty: The missing interfaces are: per-request requester/access-type at DS; comp-side current W owner/missing payload/frontier; source-R visibility; shared MIG/interconnect admission. Potential new observability or tagging is noted, but this worker does not conclude that it is an innovation.

findings.title: Decisive non-conclusions from supplied evidence
findings.claim: Several tempting conclusions are not supported by the supplied files: DS priority did not prove MIG FIFO behavior; PTE returns cannot be treated as payload credit; model DS-priority success cannot explain board PN; and ordinary strong controls often already reach comparable bounds.
evidence: docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:54: a DeepSeek counterexample mixed PTE return credit with the payload pool and misread safe p=0 fallback as a universal prohibition; it was rejected as proof of platform reachability. A proposed shared PTE-payload pool and 5% area gate were not adopted.

docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:50,63: G/H are not established as independent innovations; without a witness of a different decision under same information/resource, G/H main contribution should stop; no production RTL/BIT expansion is justified.

docs/composition-history-isolation-20261007.md:131: current V9 lacks PTW occupancy and page-table AR/R independent timing counters; sharedAWwait only counts tr-entry valid && !ready; board evidence cannot alone prove MIG return FIFO or PTE blocked by data burst.

docs/translation-lane-and-burst-rule-20261008.md:24,26: §29 local DS AR-to-first-R latency is identical at 32 cycles and A PTW-active identical at 13489, yet PN remains slower; the CPU-like synthetic read count changes with closed-loop service and no causal intervention was done, so bandwidth saturation is not established.

docs/committed-write-drain-boundary-20261008.md:26: because ordinary strong control already reaches the minimum subsequent data work in two observed cases, that step cannot establish an independent new mechanism.
docs/committed-write-drain-boundary-20261008.md:30: limits exclude partial strobe, unequal W ordering, fault/invalidation, fairness, multi-bank, hard real-time, and general cycle bounds.
findings.uncertainty: These are limits on what the supplied evidence proves, not claims that all alternatives are impossible. Additional exact source files and targeted handshake observability are required before any root wait-chain-service mechanism can be judged.
